units.text: INT. SEAGULL - CONTINUOUS
You are pig-headed! Can’t you see I want to live?
units.name: SORIN

units.text: That is futile. Nature has commanded that every life shall come to an end.
units.name: DORN

units.text: You speak like a man who is satiated with life. Your thirst for it is quenched, and so you are calm and indifferent, but even you dread death.
units.name: SORIN

units.text: The fear of death is an animal passion which must be overcome. Only those who believe in a future life and tremble for sins committed, can logically fear death; but you, for one thing, don’t believe in a future life, and for another, you haven’t committed any sins. You have served as a Councillor for twenty-five years, that is all.
units.name: DORN

units.text: Laughing.
Twenty-eight years!
units.name: SORIN

units.text: TREPLIEFF comes in and sits down on a stool at SORIN’S feet.
MASHA fixes her eyes on his face and never once tears them away.
We are keeping Constantine from his work.
units.name: DORN

units.text: No matter.
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: A pause.
Of all the cities you visited when you were abroad, Doctor, which one did you like the best?
units.name: MEDVIEDENKO

units.text: Genoa.
units.name: DORN

units.text: Why Genoa?
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: Because there is such a splendid crowd in its streets. When you leave the hotel in the evening, and throw yourself into the heart of that throng, and move with it without aim or object, swept along, hither and thither, their life seems to be yours, their soul flows into you, and you begin to believe at last in a great world spirit, like the one in your play that Nina Zarietchnaya acted. By the way, where is Nina now? Is she well?
units.name: DORN

units.text: I believe so.
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: I hear she has led rather a strange life; what happened?
units.name: DORN

units.text: It is a long story, Doctor.
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: Tell it shortly.
units.name: DORN

units.text: A pause.
She ran away from home and joined Trigorin; you know that?
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: Yes.
units.name: DORN

units.text: She had a child that died. Trigorin soon tired of her and returned to his former ties, as might have been expected. He had never broken them, indeed, but out of weakness of character had always vacillated between the two. As far as I can make out from what I have heard, Nina’s domestic life has not been altogether a success.
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: What about her acting?
units.name: DORN

units.text: I believe she made an even worse failure of that. She made her debut on the stage of the Summer Theatre in Moscow, and afterward made a tour of the country towns. At that time I never let her out of my sight, and wherever she went I followed. She always attempted great and difficult parts, but her delivery was harsh and monotonous, and her gestures heavy and crude. She shrieked and died well at times, but those were but moments.
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: Then she really has a talent for acting?
units.name: DORN

units.text: I never could make out. I believe she has. I saw her, but she refused to see me, and her servant would never admit me to her rooms. I appreciated her feelings, and did not insist upon a meeting.
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: A pause.

What more can I tell you? She sometimes writes to me now that I have come home, such clever, sympathetic letters, full of warm feeling. She never complains, but I can tell that she is profoundly unhappy; not a line but speaks to me of an aching, breaking nerve. She has one strange fancy; she always signs herself “The Sea-gull.” The miller in “Rusalka” called himself “The Crow,” and so she repeats in all her letters that she is a sea-gull. She is here now.
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: What do you mean by “here?”
units.name: DORN

units.text: In the village, at the inn. She has been there for five days. I should have gone to see her, but Masha here went, and she refuses to see any one. Some one told me she had been seen wandering in the fields a mile from here yesterday evening.
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: Yes, I saw her. She was walking away from here in the direction of the village. I asked her why she had not been to see us. She said she would come.
units.name: MEDVIEDENKO

units.text: But she won’t.
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: A pause.
Her father and stepmother have disowned her. They have even put watchmen all around their estate to keep her away.
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: He goes with the doctor toward the desk.
How easy it is, Doctor, to be a philosopher on paper, and how difficult in real life!
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: She was a beautiful girl. Even the State Councillor himself was in love with her for a time.
units.name: SORIN

units.text: You old Lovelace, you!
units.name: DORN

units.text: SHAMRAEFF’S laugh is heard.
They are coming back from the station.
units.name: PAULINA

units.text: Yes, I hear my mother’s voice.
units.name: TREPLIEFF

units.text: ARKADINA and TRIGORIN come in, followed by SHAMRAEFF.
We all grow old and wither, my lady, while you alone, with your light dress, your gay spirits, and your grace, keep the secret of eternal youth.
units.name: SHAMRAEFF

units.text: You are still trying to turn my head, you tiresome old man.
units.name: ARKADINA

units.text: To SORIN.
